I will think through this year plain and simple, the way I always do.

My land is 16.1 mu total. I have been doing cotton on most of it for many years, and the last few years I started some stevia because the company sends people to buy the dry leaves and the price is alright. This year I will keep about 12 mu in cotton and 4.1 mu in stevia. My back is not what it was, and stevia needs a lot of hand work at cutting time — 4 mu is as much as my wife and I can manage without hiring too many people.

**Cotton (12 mu):**
Last year I got about 240 kg seed cotton per mu. Not bad, not great. I use the Bt cotton seed (抗虫棉) — everyone around here does, because without it the bollworm eats you alive. I buy the seed from the same dealer in town, the improved variety.

For fertilizer, I do what I always do: one bag of compound fertilizer (45% , 15-15-15) per mu as base before planting, that's 50 kg. Then at flowering I topdress urea, about 15 kg per mu. If I count it up, that gives me about 18 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K per mu. My neighbor Old Wang adds a bit of potash at boll-forming because he says it makes the bolls bigger — I will do the same, maybe 5 kg more K per mu. Better to spend a few yuan extra than see small bolls.

Water: I pump from the well. Cotton I water maybe 3 times — once after planting if rain is short, once at flowering, once at boll filling. We've had dry springs lately.

Spraying: cotton needs a lot of spray even with Bt seed. Aphids, mirid bugs, spider mites — I spray maybe 8 or 9 times through the season. That is the biggest nuisance but you can't skip it.

Tillage: I plough in autumn after pulling the stalks, then rotary in spring before planting. Plough is important — the soil gets hard otherwise.

**Stevia (4.1 mu):**
Stevia is different. The company gave us a little training when they first brought the seedlings, so I learned some from them. It is a leaf crop, so it wants more nitrogen but not too much or the leaves go bitter and the sweet part drops. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at transplant, then topdress urea after each cutting — I cut twice, sometimes three times if the weather holds. That comes to about 20 kg N, 7 kg P, 8 kg K per mu across the season.

Stevia needs water more than cotton. I irrigate 5 times, maybe 6. After each cutting it needs a good drink to push new leaves.

Pests on stevia are less than cotton — I spray maybe 3 times, mostly for aphids and some leaf worms.

Tillage: rotary only, because I keep the crowns in the ground and just refresh between seasons.

Yield: last year I got around 350 kg dry leaf per mu. I hope for similar this year.
